subject: Fleet runway & commit ask — Corevert AI (weekly sync)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.in>
To: Nora Chen <nora.chen@corevert.ai>, Corevert Sales Team <sales@corevert.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.in>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.in>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.in>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.in>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@corevert.ai>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fleet runway & commit ask — Corevert AI (weekly sync)

Hi Nora / Corevert team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our pilot conversations and the usage profile you shared, we’ve modeled the expected token volumes and tail latency requirements for the first 90 days. Attached is a short Memo of Proposal (corevert_mop_v2.pdf) and the working GPU runway model (gpu_runway_model.csv).

High level ask for this week’s planning: can you confirm whether you’re able to convert the pilot into a 90-day reserved commitment (target start: 2027-06-01)? If so, we need a nominal commit level by next Wednesday (2027-04-28) to ensure we can allocate the Dedicated slots in the May procurement window. Without a 90-day commit, we can support Corevert on Hosted capacity but with lower burst guarantees and higher per-token unit cost.

Quick summary from our modeling:
- Nominal baseline: 8 reserved G5-like slots (continuous) to meet median throughput.
- Burst capacity: an extra 4 slots for peak window (evenings PST), configured as burst-eligible Dedicated pool.
- Economies: Reserved commitment reduces unit cost ~28% vs burst-hosted pricing.

Action items for Corevert to confirm:
1) Probability of close by 2027-05-05 (Committed / Highly Likely / Evaluate longer).
2) Any procurement constraints (PO timeline, required paperwork).
3) Preferred start date and whether partial phasing is acceptable.

Internal recipients — finance and infra, please review the attached runway model and flag any constraints on slot allocation if Corevert marks this as committed.

Thanks,

Grace O'Connor
Account Manager, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: corevert_mop_v2.pdf (proposal), gpu_runway_model.csv (workbook)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.in>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.in>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.in>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.in>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.in>
Cc: Nora Chen <nora.chen@corevert.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet runway & commit ask — Corevert AI (weekly sync)

Grace / team —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. I reviewed the runway model and ran a quick cost delta for the baseline + burst scenario. A few notes: 

- For a 90-day reserved commitment at the baseline of 8 slots, finance sees a clear unit-cost improvement (approx -28% in compute unit spend) but billing needs a signed SOW that confirms start date and monthly commit amount.
- If Corevert opts for phasing (4 slots day-one, 4 slots on day 31), we can model an amortized onboarding credit to smooth FYQ2 spend — recommend including that as an explicit line in the MOP.
- Procurement items we need from Corevert: vendor form, PO cadence (monthly vs net-30), and any additional tax/exemption docs.

Marcus — from an infra perspective, do we have capacity in the June cadence to hit a 2027-06-01 start if they confirm by 2027-04-28? If not, we need to escalate to the reserve buffer.

Grace — I’ll prepare a short contractual checklist for Nora to accelerate procurement.

Laura Bennett
Senior Finance Partner, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick infra note from my side:

- We currently have two candidate racks in the West region that can host the 8 baseline slots without impacting other reserved commitments, but that assumes no unplanned retirements in May.
- If Corevert chooses the burst + baseline model we should reserve the burst capacity as soft credits (non-blocking) so we don’t starve other high-touch customers.
- If Laura needs guarantees on availability for June start, we’ll need the week-of-2027-05-10 slot carve-out decision to lock in procurement.

Kimberly — can you add a one-pager on the burst SLAs (latency and preemption windows) to Grace's MOP?

Aditya Rao

Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet runway & commit ask — Corevert AI (weekly sync)

Hi Grace / Redwood team —

Appreciate the clear model. Internal update: our execs greenlit moving from pilot to a 90-day reserved commitment under the phased approach (4 + 4). Procurement is ready to share PO templates and vendor forms — procurement@corevert.ai will send by EOD 2027-04-28. We’re targeting a formal start of 2027-06-01, with a preference to flip baseline to full 8 slots on day 31.

A couple clarifying questions before we sign: 
1) Will Redwood provide an onboarding throughput window to validate peak traffic for 72 hours post-start?
2) In the event we exceed baseline sustained usage, what’s the short-notice scale-up lead time?

We attached a one-line term: Corevert requests the first month’s reserved slot invoice to be pro-rated to reflect the phased start.

Nora Chen
VP, Product
Corevert AI

Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet runway & commit ask — Corevert AI (weekly sync)

Nora — fantastic, thanks for the quick turnaround and for confirming the phased 90-day commitment. Recap and next steps: 

Decisions agreed:
- Corevert will sign a 90-day reserved commitment for baseline of 8 Dedicated slots, phased as 4 slots immediate + 4 slots at day 31.
- Start date: 2027-06-01. Pro-rated first invoice to reflect phase-in.
- Onboarding: Redwood will enable a 72-hour onboarding throughput validation window post-start.
- Short-notice scale: we can burst additional soft slots within 48 hours subject to rack/region constraints; hard-provisioning of extra reserved slots requires 2–3 weeks procurement lead.

Action items and owners (deadline in parentheses):
1) Corevert procurement to send PO + vendor forms (Procurement Ops) (2027-04-28).
2) Laura to produce SOW checklist + pro-rate invoice template (2027-04-29).
3) Aditya / Marcus to candidate and lock two racks; confirm slot carve-out by 2027-05-10.
4) Kimberly to add burst SLA one-pager to the MOP and attach to the HubSpot deal (2027-04-29).
5) Grace to assemble final MOP and circulate DocuSign link (2027-04-30).

I’ve uploaded the working MOP to our shared Drive and added the HubSpot deal link in Related Links.

Thanks everyone — I’ll follow up with the DocuSign and the internal capacity-lock note once Aditya confirms the racks.

Best,

Grace O'Connor
Account Manager, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
